cases.input:
A ready, privately held permit-outcome candidate predicts eventual approval when each application is submitted. Licensing and useful purpose are documented. The current snapshot contains application time, applicant features and current_status. A copied builder does this:

def build(source):
    rows = [r for r in source if r.current_status in ("approved", "rejected")]
    train, evaluation, holdout = split_by_submission_date(rows)
    write_artifact(train, evaluation, holdout)
    train_rate = sum(r.label for r in train) / len(train)
    refs = {"majority_class_accuracy": train_rate,
            "identity_auc": auc([r.label for r in evaluation], fitted_scores(train, evaluation))}
    write_summary(refs)
    write_quality({"timing": {"row_selection": {"fields": ["submission_date"],
        "basis": "only application-time eligibility; pending outcomes are unobserved targets"}}})

The wrapper is `set -eu; python3 build.py; python3 qualify_dataset.py /output/extract --report /output/q.json; python3 score.py /output/extract`. The old smoke test asserts its expected summary keys and passes; the script came from a previous candidate with recorded metrics. A colleague proposes moving write_summary after the gate, retaining the metric calculation, and then launching because a gate failure will stop final reporting. No new worker has launched, and no artifact has a passing current report. Existing tools support full qualification and --accept on workers. Provide a concrete prelaunch review and ordered repair/handoff. You cannot run tools in this exercise. Do not infer source guarantees from field names.
